guard: closeFailedBind's layered fallback (drain, then transport.close/disconnect) must actually run when nc.close() throws, so the broker's /varz.connections returns to 0 after a bind failure whose close leg rejects
why: ANCHOR ON CODE ONLY. The fixture census (bin/smoke/mutation-fixtures.smoke.ts) reddens a `find` that
spans a comment line, because prose is what anyone tidies. The explanatory comments for the three
layers therefore sit ABOVE the code span in endpoint.ts, and the anchor below is the contiguous
comment-free code from the fast-path try through the transport-destroy block. mutation-proof
matches `find` verbatim (before.split(find)), so the span must stay contiguous in the source.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, and it is the reason the command builds core first. The suite imports
CotalEndpoint from ../src/index.js. Under tsx that resolves through the workspace tsconfig
to source, so a mutation on packages/core/src/endpoint.ts is what the run sees. But the
smoke-kit peer import above resolves through pnpm's exports at @cotal-ai/core, which points
at dist/. Building core first pins both resolutions at the same source. afterRestore
rebuilds so dist/ does not stay compiled from the mutant when the next graded suite runs.
THE MUTATION IS THE PRE-REPAIR CODE, restored verbatim rather than approximated. Before the
fix, closeFailedBind swallowed a throwing close() with a bare catch and had no fallback.
The reviewer measured that state at head 52458e78e and printed after: 1 on the CLOSE-THROWS
probe. This mutation reproduces that state by replacing the whole layered teardown (fast
path, drain layer, transport-destroy layer) with the original swallow-only catch. The
multi-line find is deliberate: a single-line anchor on the fast-path catch alone would leave
TypeScript's flow analysis reading the drain and transport-destroy blocks as reachable after
an always-returning try/catch, and the build would refuse the mutant on unrelated narrowing
errors before the suite could grade anything. The tool would then report died-before-grading
and the mutation would be a lie about the invariant. Removing the whole fallback avoids that.
The CLOSE-THROWS cell must kill it. The probe injects a throwing close on the LIVE nc, so
the pre-repair catch swallows and returns without any drain or transport-destroy, and the
broker's /varz.connections stays at 1 after the failed attempt.
WHAT THIS PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It proves the CLOSE-THROWS cell REACHES the fallback
and depends on it running to bring the socket down. It does not prove the fallback's
individual layers (drain first, then transport.close, then transport.disconnect) are each
necessary. A mutation aimed at each layer in isolation is a coverage question, not a bug
question: nats.js chooses which layer resolves first at runtime and pinning a single layer
here would grade the pinned version's internals rather than the invariant. Stated so a
reader does not read the single mutation as a coverage claim it does not make.
